# Friedrich Nietzsche quote sources

9 passages attributed to Friedrich Nietzsche in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Nietzsche.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Friedrich Nietzsche

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

German

Cited here from

The Gay Science (§276, §341), Twilight of the Idols (Maxims and Arrows §8), Thus Spoke Zarathustra, and Ecce Homo.

How to cite it

Named work, numbered section (the §), and the translator. Nietzsche's sections are short and often self-contained, so a section number is a precise locator — but the English wording changes a great deal between the Kaufmann and Hollingdale translations.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

Nietzsche did not publish a book called The Will to Power. It is a compilation assembled by his sister Elisabeth Förster-Nietzsche from the notebooks, and its contents and arrangement are editorial. Any quotation sourced to it is citing an editor's construction, and the same problem affects early German editions of works he did publish.

5 of the passages below have been worked through against the cited edition, with the original-language wording and the circulating variants recorded on their own pages.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where can I check quotations attributed to Friedrich Nietzsche?

Named work, numbered section (the §), and the translator. Nietzsche's sections are short and often self-contained, so a section number is a precise locator — but the English wording changes a great deal between the Kaufmann and Hollingdale translations. This archive cites Friedrich Nietzsche from The Gay Science (§276, §341), Twilight of the Idols (Maxims and Arrows §8), Thus Spoke Zarathustra, and Ecce Homo. Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

### What is the most common mistake when quoting Friedrich Nietzsche?

Nietzsche did not publish a book called The Will to Power. It is a compilation assembled by his sister Elisabeth Förster-Nietzsche from the notebooks, and its contents and arrangement are editorial. Any quotation sourced to it is citing an editor's construction, and the same problem affects early German editions of works he did publish.

### What language did Friedrich Nietzsche write in?

German. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
